title: HyperLoRA full factor generation versus Mirror code over shared LoRA factors
hypothesis: For client LoRA updates on a shared rank-2 modulation orbit, a one-phase Mirror code over shared U,V factors matches client-conditioned full LoRA generation at lower bytes; generic two-coefficient controls may explain the result.
physical_object: shared base W0 and rank-2 LoRA factor bank U,V
mirror_coordinate: one client phase phi producing diagonal coefficients cos(phi),sin(phi)
logical_multiplicity: client-specific low-rank updates for unseen clients
controls: shared U,V plus direct two coefficients
HyperLoRA-style MLP 2->32->32 outputs full A and B factors
independent per-client rank-2 LoRA fitted using support data
gauge_rule: Compare effective delta D=A@B and function outputs; never compare raw factor coordinates as unique task codes.

development.selection_metric: held-out prediction MSE, effective delta MSE, actual bytes and compute

storage.authority: actual deterministic serialized inference payload bytes
paid_objects: shared LoRA factors or hypernetwork parameters

success_gate: Mirror test MSE <=1e-3, <=0.80x HyperLoRA payload and <=0.90x generic coefficient payload at comparable quality.
failure_gate: Generic coefficient control is within 5% bytes and quality, or Mirror misses the quality gate.
boundaries: synthetic circular rank-2 LoRA update orbit
no real federated framework or privacy evaluation
